source.title: Some of my favorite open problems

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit ball in R^3 and let λ1 = π^2 be the first eigenvalue of -Δ on Ω with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. For 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4, does the boundary value problem -Δu = u^5 + λu in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit a smooth nontrivial solution u not identically zero?
accepted.context_brief: Critical Sobolev exponent equation in 3D

evidence.quote: Let Ω be the unit ball in R3. Consider the equation (1.1) -Δu = u5 + λu in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where the unknown u : Ω → R is a smooth function and λ ∈ R is a parameter.
Open Problem 1.1 (implicit in ([BrNi1]). Assume that (1.2) 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4. Does there exist a solution u 6≡ 0 of (1.1)?

accepted.question_text: For the same unit-ball problem -Δu = u^5 + λu in Ω ⊂ R^3 with zero Dirichlet boundary condition, sign-changing solution branches are known to emanate from eigenvalues associated with nonradial sign-changing eigenfunctions when λ ≥ λ1. Do any such branches reach the interval 0 < λ < λ1/4, or must they instead have vertical asymptotes at values λ ≥ λ1/4?
accepted.context_brief: Bifurcation branches for the critical equation

evidence.quote: When λ ≥ λ1 there exist sign-changing solutions of (1.1) - but no solution u > 0 of (1.1), (see [Co]). In the bifurcation diagram, branches of solutions emanate from the eigenvalues associated with non-radial sign-changing eigenfunctions. It would be interesting to decide whether such branches “reach” the interval (0, λ1/4); they might instead admit e.g. vertical asymptotes at values of λ ≥ λ1/4.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disk in R^2 and ε > 0. Consider the Ginzburg-Landau system -Δu = ε^{-2}u(1 - |u|^2) in Ω with boundary condition u(x) = x on ∂Ω, where u maps Ω into R^2. The radial solution Uε is defined by Uε(x) = x|x|^{-1} fε(|x|), where fε solves the corresponding radial ODE with fε(0)=0 and fε(1)=1. Is Uε the only solution of this boundary value problem?
accepted.context_brief: Uniqueness of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution

evidence.quote: We will denote by Uε(x) the solution of (2.1) given by (2.2)-(2.3), and we call it the radially symmetric (or just the radial) solution of (2.1). A long-standing open problem is whether Uε(x) is also the unique solution of (2.1): Open Problem 2.1 ([BBH, Problem 10 in Chapter XI]). Is the radial solution Uε the only solution of (2.1)?

accepted.question_text: Find a simpler proof of the theorem of Pacard and Rivière asserting that, for sufficiently small ε > 0, the radial solution Uε is the unique solution of the disk Ginzburg-Landau system -Δu = ε^{-2}u(1 - |u|^2), u=x on ∂Ω.
accepted.context_brief: Simpler proof for small-ε Ginzburg-Landau uniqueness

evidence.quote: When ε is sufficiently small: ε < ε0 for some appropriate ε0. This result is due to Pacard-Rivi`ere [PR]. Their proof is highly non-trivial and fills a significant part of the monograph [PR]; it would be interesting to find a simpler proof.

accepted.question_text: For the disk Ginzburg-Landau energy Eε(u) = (1/2)∫Ω |∇u|^2 + (1/(4ε^2))∫Ω (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on H^1_g(Ω; R^2), where g(x)=x on ∂Ω, is the radial solution Uε a minimizer of Eε for every ε > 0?
accepted.context_brief: Global minimality of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution

evidence.quote: Note that (2.1) has a variational structure: the solutions of (2.1) are the critical points of the Ginzburg-Landau energy. Eε(u) := 1/2 ∫Ω |∇u|2 + 1/(4ε2) ∫Ω (|u|2 − 1)2, subject to the boundary condition u ∈ H1g(Ω; R2), where g(x) = x on ∂Ω.
Open Problem 2.2. Is Uε a minimizer of Eε on H1g(Ω; R2) for any ε > 0?

accepted.question_text: Let p > 2 and let Ω be the unit disk in R^2 with boundary condition g(x)=x on ∂Ω. For the p-Ginzburg-Landau energy Eε,p(u) = (1/p)∫Ω |∇u|^p + (1/(4ε^2))∫Ω (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on W^{1,p}_g(Ω; R^2), if uε is any minimizer or any critical point, does uε(x) converge to x/|x| for every x in Ω \ {0} as ε → 0?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic radial symmetry for p-Ginzburg-Landau

evidence.quote: One can also raise identical questions for the p−GL energy Eε,p(u) := 1/p ∫Ω |∇u|p + 1/(4ε2) ∫Ω (|u|2 − 1)2, where p > 1, Ω is the unit disc in R2 and u ∈ W1,p g(Ω; R2), with g(x) = x on ∂Ω.
Open Problem 2.3 ([BM, Open Problem 30]). Assume p > 2 and let uε be any minimizer (resp. critical point) of Eε,p on W1,p g(Ω, R2). Does uε(x) → x/|x| in Ω \ {0} as ε → 0?

accepted.question_text: Consider smooth maps u: R^2 → R^2 ≃ C satisfying the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation -Δu = u(1 - |u|^2) on R^2 and the condition |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞. The degree at infinity deg(u,∞) is then defined, and for each integer q there is a distinguished radial-equivariant solution Vq(r,θ)=e^{iqθ}gq(r), with V0 ≡ 1 and deg(Vq,∞)=q. Must every such solution u be equal, up to multiplication by a complex unit and translation in R^2, to Vq with q = deg(u,∞)?
accepted.context_brief: Classification of entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem is whether the functions Vq, q ∈ Z, are the only solutions of (2.5)-(2.6). More precisely Open Problem 2.4 ([BBH, Problem 14], [BMR], [Br3]). Let u be any solution of (2.5) - (2.6). Does u coincide with Vq modulo rotation and translation, where q = deg(u, ∞)? I.e., is u(x) = αVq(x − x0) for some α ∈ C, |α| = 1, and x0 ∈ R2?

accepted.question_text: For any smooth solution u: R^2 → R^2 of the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation -Δu = u(1 - |u|^2) satisfying |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞, must the potential-energy integral ∫_{R^2} (|u|^2 - 1)^2 be finite?
accepted.context_brief: Finite potential energy for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions

evidence.quote: and which satisfies in addition (2.11) ∫R2 (|u|2 − 1)2 < ∞.
Open Problem 2.5 ([BMR, Problem 2], [Br3, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.5) and (2.6). Does (2.11) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disk in R^2, let 0 < R < 1, and prescribe the boundary map g(x,y)=(Rx,Ry,√(1-R^2)) from ∂Ω into S^2. For harmonic maps u: Ω → S^2 solving -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|^2 in Ω with u=g on ∂Ω, two explicit solutions u and ū are known and are the unique minimizers in the relevant degree classes E0 and E_{-1}. Are there any other solutions of this harmonic-map boundary value problem besides those two explicit solutions?
accepted.context_brief: Additional harmonic maps from the disk to S^2

evidence.quote: Consider the boundary condition (3.6) g(x, y) = (Rx, Ry, √1 − R2) for (x, y) ∈ ∂Ω, with 0 < R < 1. In this case one can write down two explicit solutions of (3.1)-(3.3).
This does not exclude the possible existence of other solutions of (3.1)-(3.3): Open Problem 3.1 ([BrCo]). Assume g is given by (3.6). Are there other solutions of (3.1)-(3.3) besides u and ¯u?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω = B^3 be the unit ball in R^3 and let g: ∂Ω ≃ S^2 → S^2 be a smooth boundary map of degree zero. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map u: Ω → S^2 satisfying -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|^2 for i=1,2,3 in Ω, |u(x)|=1 in Ω, and u=g on ∂Ω?
accepted.context_brief: Continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2

evidence.quote: Since we will be concerned with the existence of continuous harmonic maps satisfying (4.3) we assume throughout this section that (4.6) deg g = 0. Here is a long-standing open problem originally posed by R. Schoen in the mid-1980’s: Open Problem 4.1 ([HaLi], [Ha], [Br5, Open Problem 3]). Assume that (4.6) holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)-(4.3)?

accepted.question_text: In the degree-zero boundary setting for harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2, consider the infimum of the Dirichlet energy E(u)=∫Ω |∇u|^2 over maps u in H^1_g(Ω;S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball. Is this infimum achieved by some continuous map?
accepted.context_brief: Energy minimization among continuous harmonic-map competitors

evidence.quote: In order to solve Open Problem 4.1 it is tempting to tackle Open Problem 4.2 ([HaLi], [Ha]). Is the (4.8) Inf {E(u); u ∈ H1g(Ω; S2) ∩ C(Ω)} achieved?

accepted.question_text: In the degree-zero harmonic-map setting from B^3 to S^2, can it happen that no minimizer exists for the energy infimum over continuous competitors, yet a continuous harmonic map with the prescribed boundary data still exists?
accepted.context_brief: Possible separation between existence and continuous minimization

evidence.quote: Clearly, a positive answer to Open Problem 4.2 would provide a solution to Open Problem 4.1. But in principle it might happen that the answer to Open Problem 4.2 is negative while the answer to Problem 4.1 is positive. (Can this scenario occcur?)

accepted.question_text: For harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 with degree-zero boundary data, define the relaxed energy R on H^1_g(Ω;S^2) through weak H^1 limits of continuous maps. Are the minimizers of this relaxed energy continuous on the closed ball, or is at least one relaxed-energy minimizer continuous?
accepted.context_brief: Continuity of relaxed-energy minimizers

evidence.quote: Therefore prospective solutions of Open Problem 4.2 are to be found among the minimizers of (4.10). This leads us to Open Problem 4.3 ([BBC]). Are the minimizers of (4.10) continuous on Ω? (Is it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

accepted.question_text: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed energy R for H^1_g(Ω;S^2) maps in the degree-zero B^3 setting, and let S(u) be the singular-interaction term in the representation R(u)=∫Ω|∇u|^2+S(u), equivalently encoded by the distributional Jacobian Ju. Must S(u)=0, equivalently Ju=0, or equivalently must there exist continuous maps un in H^1_g(Ω;S^2) converging strongly to u in H^1?
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing singular interaction for relaxed-energy minimizers

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.4. Let u be a minimizer of (4.10). Is it true that S(u) = 0, i.e., Ju = 0 ? or equivalently that there exists a sequence (un) in H1g(Ω; S2) ∩ C(Ω) such that un converges to u strongly in H1?

accepted.question_text: For maps f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1), 1 < p ≤ 2, does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| is bounded by c(p-1) times the double integral over S^1×S^1 of |f(x)-f(y)|^p/|x-y|^2?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp p→1 degree estimate

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.1 ([Br7, Remark 7]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that, for every 1 < p ≤ 2, (5.6) | deg f| ≤ c(p − 1) ∫S1∫S1 |f(x) − f(y)|p/|x − y|2 ∀f ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1)?

accepted.question_text: For continuous maps f:S^1→S^1, Theorem 5.2 states that |deg f| is bounded by a constant C times the double integral of |x-y|^{-2} over pairs (x,y) with |f(x)-f(y)| ≥ √3. Is there a simpler and more geometric proof of this theorem, what is the best possible constant C, and is that best constant achieved?
accepted.context_brief: Geometric proof and sharp constant for a degree estimate

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.2. There exists a constant C such that for every f ∈ C(S1; S1) (5.9) | deg f| ≤ C ∫S1∫S1 [|f(x)−f(y)|≥√3] dxdy/|x − y|2.
Open Problem 5.2 ([BM, Open Problem 18]). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of Theorem 5.2? What is the best constant C in (5.9)? Is it achieved?

accepted.question_text: For f in C(S^1;S^1) and δ>0, let Iδ(f) be the double integral of |x-y|^{-2} over pairs (x,y) in S^1×S^1 such that |f(x)-f(y)| ≥ δ. Does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| ≤ c δ Iδ(f) for every continuous f:S^1→S^1 and every δ ≤ √3?
accepted.context_brief: Small-threshold improvement for degree estimates

evidence.quote: Given f ∈ C(S1; S1) and δ > 0, set (5.10) Iδ(f) := ∫S1∫S1 [|f(x)−f(y)|≥δ] dxdy/|x − y|2.
Open Problem 5.3 ([Br7, Open Problem 3]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that (5.12) | deg f| ≤ cδIδ(f) ∀f ∈ C(S1; S1) ∀δ ≤ √3?

accepted.question_text: For 1 < p < ∞ and integer d, let mp,d be the infimum of the p-th W^{1/p,p} seminorm among maps f:S^1→S^1 of degree d. Is mp,d = |d| mp,1 for every d? Is the infimum defining mp,d achieved? If this linear formula fails, is there an explicit formula for lim_{d→∞} mp,d/d = inf_{d>0} mp,d/d?
accepted.context_brief: Minimal nonlocal energy in a prescribed degree class

evidence.quote: given 1 < p < ∞ and d ∈ Z set (5.13) mp,d := Inf {|f|p W1/p,p ; f ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1), deg f = d}.

Open Problem 5.4 ([BM, Open Problems 22 and 23]). Let 1 < p < ∞. Is true that (5.15) mp,d = |d|mp,1 ∀d ∈ Z? Is the inf in (5.13) achieved? The answer to both questions is positive for p = 2. Assuming that (5.15) does not hold, is there an explicit formula for (5.16) lim d→+∞ mp,d/d = inf d>0 mp,d/d?

accepted.question_text: Find a simpler construction of continuous maps f,g:S^1→S^1 with identical Fourier-modulus data |an(f)|=|an(g)| for every n∈Z but different degrees.
accepted.context_brief: Simpler counterexample to hearing the degree

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.4 ([BoKo]). There exist two functions f, g ∈ C(S1; S1) such that |an(f)| = |an(g)| ∀n ∈ Z, and deg f 6= deg g. The construction of Bourgain-Kozma in [BoKo] is quite elaborate and it would be desirable to find a simpler one.

accepted.question_text: Suppose f,g:S^1→S^1 have equal Fourier coefficient moduli |an(f)|=|an(g)| for every n∈Z. The equality deg f=deg g is known when f,g ∈ W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1), and also for Hölder maps of exponent α>1/3. Does the same conclusion hold when f,g ∈ W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) with p>3, or when f,g are Hölder with exponent α≤1/3? What happens under the asymmetric stronger assumptions f ∈ W^{1/p,p}, 2<p≤3, g ∈ W^{1/q,q}, q>3, or f ∈ C^{0,α}, α>1/3, g ∈ C^{0,β}, β≤1/3?
accepted.context_brief: Borderline regularity for hearing the degree

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.5 ([Br7, Corollary 2], [BM, Corollary 12.3], [Ka]). Assume that f, g ∈ W1/3,3(S1; S1) satisfy |an(f)| = |an(g)| ∀n ∈ Z, then deg f = deg g. In particular the conclusion holds if f, g ∈ C0,α(S1; S1) with α > 1/3.

Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f, g ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1) with p > 3 (resp. f, g ∈ C0,α(S1: S1) with α ≤ 1/3)? The problem is open even under the stronger assumption that f ∈ W1/p,p with 2 < p ≤ 3 and g ∈ W1/q,q with q > 3 (resp. f ∈ C0,α with α > 1/3 and g ∈ C0,β with β ≤ 1/3).

accepted.question_text: For p>3, or for a Hölder exponent α≤1/3, does there exist a summation process σ_{n,ε}, depending only on p or only on α, such that for every f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1), respectively every f in C^{0,α}(S^1;S^1), the limit as ε→0 of Σ_{n∈Z} n |an(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε} equals deg f? A summation process means σ_{n,ε} has sup_n |n||σ_{n,ε}|<∞ for each ε∈(0,1) and σ_{n,ε}→1 for each fixed n.
accepted.context_brief: Degree recovery from Fourier magnitudes by summation

evidence.quote: by a summation process we mean a family (σn,ε), n ∈ Z, 0 < ε < 1, satisfying: (5.23) ∀ε ∈ (0, 1), sup n∈Z |n||σn,ε| < ∞, (5.24) ∀n ∈ Z, lim ε&0 σn,ε = 1.
Open Problem 5.6. Given any p > 3 (resp. α ≤ 1/3) does there exist a summation process (σn,ε), depending only on p (resp. α) such that (5.25) holds for every f ∈ W1/p,p (resp. f ∈ C0,α)?

accepted.question_text: Given an individual map f in C(S^1;S^1), or more generally in VMO(S^1;S^1), does there exist a summation process σ_{n,ε} that may depend on f and recovers the degree from Fourier magnitudes by lim_{ε→0} Σ_{n∈Z} n |an(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε} = deg f?
accepted.context_brief: Function-dependent summation for hearing the degree

evidence.quote: In the same vein one can raise: Open Problem 5.7. Given any f ∈ C(S1; S1) (resp. f ∈ V MO(S1; S1)) does there exist a summation process (σn,ε) (depending on f) such that (5.25) holds?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a single map f in C(S^1;S^1), or in VMO(S^1;S^1), such that no summation process σ_{n,ε} can recover the degree from the Fourier magnitudes, meaning that Σ_{n∈Z} n|an(f)|^2σ_{n,ε} fails to converge to deg f for every possible summation process?
accepted.context_brief: Universal obstruction to summation-based degree recovery

evidence.quote: A stronger version of Corollary 5.1 is open: Open Problem 5.8. Does there exist some f ∈ C(S1; S1) (resp. f ∈ V MO(S1; S1)) such that for any summation process (σn,ε), Σ n∈Z n|an(f)|2σn,ε does not converge to deg f?

accepted.question_text: For maps f:S^2→S^2 in H^1, let Ed be the class of maps of degree d, and define Dist_{H^1}(Ed1,Ed2)=sup_{f∈Ed1} inf_{g∈Ed2} ||∇(f-g)||_{L^2}. Is Dist_{H^1}(Ed1,Ed2)^2 = 8π|d1-d2| for all integers d1,d2? Even more basically, is Dist_{H^1}(Ed1,Ed2)=Dist_{H^1}(Ed2,Ed1) for all d1,d2?
accepted.context_brief: Distances between H^1 homotopy classes on S^2

evidence.quote: Consider e.g. H1(S2; S2) and its homotopy classes Ed = {f ∈ H1(S2; S2); deg f = d}, d ∈ Z. The quantity of interest is DistH1 (Ed1, Ed2) = Sup f∈Ed1 Inf g∈Ed2 ||∇(f − g)||L2.

Open Problem 5.9 ([BMS]). Is true that (5.28) Dist2 H1 (Ed1, Ed2) = 8π|d1 − d2| ∀d1, d2 ∈ Z? The inequality ≤ is known, (see [BMS] and the references therein) but the reverse inequality (≥) has been established only when d2 > d1 ≥ 0. Even a much easier problem is open: Is it true that DistH1 (Ed1, Ed2) = DistH1 (Ed2, Ed1) ∀d1, d2 ∈ Z?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the closed unit ball in R^N and let f:B→B be a VMO map. Is it true that for every ε>0, the approximate fixed-point set {x∈B: |f(x)-x|<ε} has positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: VMO version of Brouwer fixed point theorem

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.10. Let B be the closed unit ball in RN and let f be a VMO map from B into itself. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the set {x ∈ B; |f(x) − x| < ε} has positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded smooth convex subset of R^N with N≥10, and consider -Δu=λe^u in Ω, u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω. Let u* be the extremal weak solution obtained as λ increases to the critical parameter λ*. Is u* unbounded? If some convex domains have bounded u* for f(u)=e^u, can one find another smooth increasing convex superlinear nonlinearity f, possibly depending on Ω and satisfying f(0)>0 and f(t)/t→∞, for which the corresponding extremal solution u* is not in L∞(Ω)?
accepted.context_brief: Unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension

evidence.quote: Consider the nonlinear elliptic equation (6.1) -Δu = λf(u) in Ω ⊂ RN, u > 0 in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where Ω is a smooth bounded domain in RN, λ > 0 is a constant, and f : [0, +∞) → (0, +∞) is a smooth function satisfying (6.2) f(0) > 0, f is increasing and convex, and (6.3) limt→∞ f(t)/t = +∞.

Open Problem 6.1 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume Ω is a bounded smooth convex set in RN, N ≥ 10. Let f(u) = eu. Is u∗ unbounded? If the answer is negative for some domains Ω, can one find other functions f satisfying (6.2)-(6.3) (possibly depending on Ω) such that u∗ ∈/ L∞(Ω)?

accepted.question_text: For the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Δu=λf(u), u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, with f satisfying f(0)>0, increasing convexity, and f(t)/t→∞, suppose the extremal solution u* is unbounded. What can be said about the blow-up set of u*? If Ω is convex, must the blow-up set consist of a single point?
accepted.context_brief: Blow-up set of an unbounded extremal solution

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.2 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume u∗ ∈/ L∞(Ω). What can be said about the blow-up set of u∗? Does it consist of a single point when Ω is convex?

accepted.question_text: On the torus T^N with N≥2, does there exist a constant C such that every test function ψ satisfies the Bourgain-Brezis type estimate ||ψ - ∫ψ||_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} ≤ C ||∇ψ||_{H^{-1/2}+L^1}? This is the strengthened estimate needed to derive the H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} phase estimate by the same duality method used for the weaker L^{N/(N-1)} estimate.
accepted.context_brief: Undecided Bourgain-Brezis estimate

evidence.quote: If we try to establish (7.8) by the same method as above we would need to invoke a stronger version of (7.6), namely (7.9) kψ − ∫ ψkH1/2+W1,1 ≤ Ck∇ψkH−1/2+L1 ∀ψ. However such an estimate is still undecided: Open Problem 7.1 ([BoBr]). Does (7.9) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in R^N, N≥2, and let f be smooth on the closure of Ω. For the Rudin-Osher-Fatemi type functional Φ(u)=∫Ω |∇u| + (1/2)∫Ω |u-f|^2 defined on BV(Ω)∩L^2(Ω), let U be its unique minimizer. Given that ∇U∈L∞(Ω) but ∇U need not be continuous, is ∇U in BV(Ω)?
accepted.context_brief: BV regularity of total-variation minimizers

evidence.quote: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in RN, N ≥ 2. Assume (for simplicity) that f is a smooth function on Ω and consider the functional Φ(u) := ∫Ω |∇u| + 1/2 ∫Ω |u − f|2 defined for u ∈ BV (Ω) ∩ L2(Ω).
The minimizer U satisfies ∇U ∈ L∞(Ω), but in general ∇U is not continuous. This still leaves room for improvement: Open Problem 8.1 ([Br10, Open Problem 1]). Does ∇U belong to BV (Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Find a more direct and elementary proof, in the spirit of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung, of the p=1 case of the theorem asserting that if a measurable u satisfies λΦ_{λ,p}(u)→0 as λ→∞, then u is constant, where Φ_{λ,p}(u) is the measure of pairs (x,y) for which |u(x)-u(y)|^p/|x-y|^{p+N} ≥ λ.
accepted.context_brief: Elementary proof for the p=1 constant-function criterion

evidence.quote: Theorem 9.1 is due to Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung [BVY] when p > 1, (with Ω = RN but the proof is unchanged when Ω is a ball), and to Poliakovsky [Pol, Corollary 1.1] when p = 1. Actually, Poliakovsky derives the result from a deeper assertion (see below); as a consequence the proof of Theorem 9.1 when p = 1 is quite intricate and it would be desirable to find a more direct and elementary proof, possibly in the spirit of [BVY].

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded connected domain in R^N, N≥1, and for a measurable u:Ω→R define Φ_{λ,p}(u) as the measure of pairs (x,y)∈Ω×Ω satisfying |u(x)-u(y)|^p/|x-y|^{p+N} ≥ λ. If liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,p}(u)=0 for some p≥1, must u be constant almost everywhere?
accepted.context_brief: Liminf version of the constant-function criterion

evidence.quote: Given λ > 0, p ≥ 1, and a measurable function u : Ω → R, set (9.2) Φλ,p(u) := meas {(x, y) ∈ Ω × Ω; |u(x) − u(y)|p/|x − y|p+N ≥ λ}.
Open Problem 9.1 ([BVY, Open Problem 1]). Assume that u satisfies (9.4) lim inf λ→∞ λΦλ,p(u) = 0 for some p ≥ 1. Can one conclude that u is a constant?

accepted.question_text: With Ω and Φ_{λ,p}(u) as above, for every 1<p<∞ does there exist C=C(p,N,Ω) such that all measurable u satisfy ||∇u||_{L^p}^p ≤ C liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,p}(u), interpreting ||∇u||_{L^p}=∞ when u∉W^{1,p}(Ω)? Similarly, for p=1 does there exist C=C(N,Ω) such that ||∇u||_M ≤ C liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,1}(u), where ||∇u||_M is total variation for BV functions and ∞ outside BV?
accepted.context_brief: Liminf control of Sobolev and BV seminorms

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.2 ([BSVY, Section 7.2]). Given any 1 < p < ∞, is there a constant C = C(p, N, Ω) such that, for all measurable functions u, (9.5) k∇ukp Lp ≤ C lim inf λ→∞ λΦλ,p(u)? in the sense that k∇ukLp = ∞ if u /∈ W1,p(Ω). Similarly for p = 1, is there a constant C = C(N, Ω) such that, for all measurable functions u, (9.6) k∇ukM ≤ C lim inf λ→∞ λΦλ,1(u)? where k∇ukM denotes the total mass of ∇u if u ∈ BV (Ω), and k∇ukM = ∞ if u /∈ BV (Ω).

accepted.question_text: Do the nonlocal functionals λΦ_{λ,p} Γ-converge as λ→∞ to the functional Ψ that equals cp||∇u||_{L^p}^p on W^{1,p}(Ω) and +∞ outside W^{1,p}(Ω) when p>1, and equals c1||∇u||_M on BV(Ω) and +∞ outside BV(Ω) when p=1, for some positive constants cp and c1?
accepted.context_brief: Gamma convergence of nonlocal Sobolev/BV approximations

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9.3 ([BSVY, Section 7.3]). Does the family of functionals λΦλ,p converge as λ → ∞, in the sense of Γ-convergence, to the functional Ψ defined, when p > 1, by Ψ(u) := cpk∇ukp Lp if u ∈ W1,p(Ω), +∞ if u /∈ W1,p(Ω), and when p = 1 by Ψ(u) := c1k∇ukM if u ∈ BV (Ω), +∞ if u /∈ BV (Ω), for some positive constants cp and c1?

accepted.question_text: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N, N≥2. For 0≤t≤1, define f_N(t) as the infimum of the relative perimeter P(S) over measurable subsets S⊂Q with volume |S|=t, where P(S) counts only boundary inside Q. An explicit formula is known for N=2. Is there a similar formula for f_N(t) when N≥3? In particular, is f_N(t) identically 1 near t=1/2?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp relative isoperimetric inequality for the cube

evidence.quote: Let Q be the unit cube in RN, N ≥ 2. Given a measurable set S ⊂ Q, denote by 1S the characteristic function of S, by |S| = k1SkL1 the volume of S, and by P(S) the relative perimeter of S, i.e., taking into account only the part of the boundary of S inside Q; in other words P(S) is the total mass of the measure ∇1S.
Open Problem 10.1 ([BreBru]). Is there a formula similar to (10.2) for fN (t) when N ≥ 3? In particular, is it true that fN (t) ≡ 1 near t = 1/2?
